newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money falls further on last day of pact.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money falls further on last day of pact.

text.p: Dutch call money fell further on Thursday while the market enjoyed the last day under the current advances pact with a generous allocation.
Dealers said trade was thin and participants continued to save under the current credit quota as a lot of liquidity was flowing into the market under the current pact.
The current eight-day advances pact with an allocation of 6.57 billion guilders will be replaced on Friday, but the Dutch central bank will announce the rate and duration this afternoon at 1500 GMT.
Dealers said the rate would remain at 2.50 percent.
Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing's remarks earlier today were ignored by the market.

Issing said there was no reason for an interest rate cut in Germany at the moment, but dealers said the market had not expected anything else after the spate of remarks from Bundesbank officials in recent weeks.
"Nothing will change in the near term," said one dealer, anticipating official rates in Germany and the Netherlands would remain unchanged for some time.
Call money rates were bid as low as 2.38 percent versus 2.50 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said call rates were likely to climb above the special advances rate after the new allocation on Friday.
Three-month deposits were glued at 2.92 percent bid.
The guilder was steady at 112.1525 per 100 marks from 112.155 on Wednesday.
